transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-10 15:30 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Hale (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Solstice Head of Security), Ethan Zhao (Platform Engineer), Marta Ruiz (Compliance), Oliver Grant (SRE)

Auto-generated Summary: (may be imperfect) Solstice is evaluating Redwood export and audit fidelity for legal/forensics needs, esp for EU data. Wants proof that admin events, token lifecycle, model access, and payload metadata are captured and can be exported with customer-managed keys.

-- Transcript Body --
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: okay hi everyone thanks for joining i'm lena from redwood uh we'll do quick intros and then jump into audit export details, sound good?
[00:06] Priya Menon: yes thanks lena um i'm priya head of security at solstice. our main ask is we need a forensics-ready trail for any admin or privileged activity.
[00:14] Marcus Hale: great, Marcus here, i'll cover the export mechanics and event taxonomy. quick note — transcription may mess up some product names.
[00:20] Ethan Zhao: hey all, ethan. operationally we run splunk on prem and want to forward logs into a dedicated index. also, EU-only archive needed.
[00:29] Marta Ruiz: compliance question: retention for default logs vs long-term legal hold? what granularity do you provide?
[00:35] Lena Ortiz: good — let's outline what redwood captures: system admin actions (user create/delete, role changes), api key creation/rotation, model inference requests metadata (not full prompt payload by default, but metadata + hash), session token issuance, console logins, and deployment rollouts. there are also audit-level traces for routing and fallback events.
[00:55] Priya Menon: when you say you don't capture full prompt payload, is that configurable? for forensics we might need the raw prompts tied to a legal case, but only under strict controls.
[01:05] Marcus Hale: yes configurable. by default we store metadata and a SHA256 prompt fingerprint to avoid storing PII, but for export we support on-demand full payload extraction if customer agrees and signs a retention + access policy. we also support redaction heuristics.
[01:20] Oliver Grant: how is that gated? via RBAC? SSO?
[01:24] Marcus Hale: RBAC controls who can trigger full exports, plus SAML SSO + SCIM groups map to roles. we have an "audit export" role that you can map to specific admins. all exports are recorded as admin events themselves.
[01:36] Ethan Zhao: for the export mechanism — is it push or pull? we want a push into our EU S3 bucket and a stream into splunk.
[01:42] Marcus Hale: we support multiple methods concurrently: scheduled S3 push (encrypted, server-side with CMK if you choose), a webhook stream for near-real-time events (TLS 1.2+), and a bulk export API for ad hoc retrieval. Splunk ingestion we recommend via a small forwarder that reads from S3 or via direct webhook to a consumer queue.
[02:01] Priya Menon: customer-managed keys — can we provide our own KMS/HSM? we need to control key rotation and ensure isolation.
[02:08] Marcus Hale: yes, we have two options: bring-your-own-key via cloud KMS (you give Redwood access to wrap/unwrap with an IAM role) or a dedicated HSM proxy for on-prem. for the private deployment we can integrate with your on-prem HSM through a secure connector. all exported archives can be encrypted with your key before leaving redwood.
[02:28] Marta Ruiz: about chain-of-custody — we need to record who exported what and when, and the exported artifact should include a digest and signed metadata. is that supported?
[02:36] Marcus Hale: accepted practice — our export bundle includes a signed manifest (we sign with our platform key) and you can request we also sign with your key in the POC. manifest includes export timestamp, event range, SHA256 checksums, and an audit_id that links back to internal event logs.
[02:53] Lena Ortiz: also note we provide tamper-evidence: every export manifest references the originating admin event id and we persist the export action in the audit store immutably.
[03:03] Ethan Zhao: Splunk — any recommended schema or parsers? we need field names to map.
[03:07] Marcus Hale: we export a JSONL line per event with fields: event_type, timestamp, user_id, role, ip, resource, action, request_id, model_id, prompt_fingerprint, retcode, and optional payload_blob (if enabled). we'll share a sample mapping for Splunk, and we can build a pipeline template that creates indices and sourcetypes.
[03:30] Priya Menon: retention defaults? we need 2 years for some records, but 90 days is fine for working copy.
[03:36] Lena Ortiz: defaults are 90 days hot storage, 1 year cold archive in EU regions, and indefinite cold storage if you opt-in (additional cost). legal holds override TTLs; we can pin exports to a legal-hold bucket.
[03:50] Oliver Grant: are exports incremental or full snapshots? we prefer incremental deltas to reduce egress.
[03:55] Marcus Hale: both — we can do daily deltas + weekly full snapshots. deltas are patch files with event ranges. we also have cursor-based streaming for near-real-time.
[04:07] Ethan Zhao: network — will you push into our VPC or do we pull? concerns about cross-region egress.
[04:12] Marcus Hale: for hosted we can push to your VPC via VPC endpoint (private link) or to your S3 with a VPC endpoint and a presigned-bucket policy. for private deployments we run inside your VPC. cross-region egress is controlled by region selection — if you select eu-west-1 we keep data in EU.
[04:28] Marta Ruiz: SOC 2 evidence: do you keep copies of access control changes, and can we get a timeline for historical roles?
[04:34] Lena Ortiz: yes, we persist role history and we can export an account-change timeline (who granted what role and when). that is part of the audit event type. we'll include that in the SOC2 evidence package.
[04:44] Priya Menon: how are secrets handled in exports — api keys in events? we don't want keys in plain text.
[04:49] Marcus Hale: secrets are redacted by default. if you require keys then we do ephemeral tokens and encrypt them in the bundle. we discourage exporting raw secrets; we provide tokenized references and remediation playbooks.
[04:59] Ethan Zhao: provable deletion — after the archive TTL, do you provide deletion receipts?
[05:03] Marcus Hale: yes we emit deletion events and signed deletion receipts; for EU data residency we can configure deletion to follow local regulations and provide an audit proof.
[05:13] Priya Menon: legal hold flow — who can lift a hold?
[05:16] Lena Ortiz: only designated compliance admins (mapped via SCIM group) can lift holds, and that action itself is an audit event requiring multi-person approval if you turn on the two-person rule.
[05:27] Oliver Grant: can we run a dry-run where redwood pushes a masked sample dataset to our EU bucket for verification?
[05:32] Marcus Hale: absolutely — that's what the POC is for. we'll push a masked sample first, then a full (if authorized). we'll document the masking pipeline and the redaction score.
[05:44] Marta Ruiz: about governance — do you support retention policies per customer, per org unit?
[05:48] Lena Ortiz: yes you can configure retention per tenant, per namespace, or per dataset via the console or API. we'll show policy json examples in the playbook.
[05:58] Ethan Zhao: any SLA for export job completion times? we're thinking of investigative cases where time-to-evidence matters.
[06:04] Marcus Hale: we have priority export tiers for dedicated customers; for hosted we provide best-effort with an SLA add-on. typical delivery for a 48-hour range is under 30 mins for deltas, longer for multi-month snapshots. dedicated capacity reduces that to sub-10 minutes for typical ranges.
[06:21] Priya Menon: compliance check — do you maintain immutable logs for admin UI as well as API?
[06:26] Marcus Hale: yes both UI and API actions are instrumented. UI actions include screen metadata (not screenshots) and effective user context.
[06:33] Lena Ortiz: quick recap — POC: masked sample push to EU S3, Splunk index plumbing, verify KMS integration, confirm legal hold workflow. next steps: we'll share SOC2 & ISO certs, policy docs, and a POC runbook.
[06:47] Ethan Zhao: sounds good. will expect the redwood runbook and sample schema.
[06:51] Priya Menon: one final — are there cross-account concerns if multiple sub-orgs request exports? can we centralize control?
[06:57] Marcus Hale: yes central admin can delegate export rights and require approvals; we support audit chains and can surface pending export requests in the console.
[07:05] Lena Ortiz: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the deep dive.

End of transcript.
